title: Across the tracks
rule: Seen from the far platform: the station a small lit box, the figures tiny in its windows, the balloons long-tailed across the rails.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: one far viewpoint repeated in all seven panels: our own platform edge (pale painted edge line) at the foot, two tracks of charcoal-card sleepers and rails between, the station a small dark card box with a hipped roof, a RANDOLPH name board and three lit windows; two torn ridges of hills, hand-cut trees and telegraph poles behind; the sky is the teuf-teuf Cueva plain-rock relief (ramp-printed) worked over with long broken charcoal strokes

the charcoal-card kit rebuilt for this page (card_k in p20_across_the_tracks.py, also used for the figures pinned by charcoal99.pin_up): every card rubbed with the foraged Cueva rock relief (charcoal99.rock_tile, CC BY-SA 3.0, Suzko) sampled at its own offset and scale, worked over with broken charcoal hatching at a hand-chosen angle, heavier toward the cut edges and in patches (lifted, eraser-like strokes on the dark cards), cut with wandering scissor facets or torn with a ragged edge and pale fibrous rim (hills, bushes, caption cards), and each dropped with its own shadow; the ballast is rock-rubbed with charcoal dabs for stones; the window light on the platform is broken by the rock and strokes

trees: varied hand-cut cards (round lobed crowns, tall poplars, tiered firs, low torn bushes) of different sizes and tones, each outline re-cut as straight scissor facets, each with its own trunk card

the lit office rendered on its own and seen only through the cut windows: the b1m2 agent at 0.14 scale (about 100 px tall) at his desk (W1), crossing past the ticket window (W2) under the office clock, and at the cupboard (W3); cupboard, its door leaf with the brass key and paper tag on its hook, and the SERVICE door with a pale card fleck, cut as plain cards at this distance
the stranger: a small back-view card puppet made for this page (hat, head, coat, skirt, legs), outside on the station platform against the lit ticket window, then walking off down the platform
panel 1 adds a big dark lamp post and bench end on our platform for scale

the four canonical lines verbatim in cut-card balloons laid on our side of the rails, their long tails running across both tracks to the tiny speaker; short captions on pale cards in the shared pen hand
hand-ruled borders (penlib.border_mask); folio '20 / Across the tracks' (pen99.folio)
the panels are softened once by 0.95 px before toning so the page stays inside the 1.2 MB JPEG budget; rock relief, strokes and card edges are 3-20 px features and survive

events.E0: P1: the agent at his desk in the left window (caption: reads his memo); P2: 4:09, he crosses past the ticket window; the stranger approaches along the far platform
events.E1: P3: the stranger at the lit ticket window; her balloon tailed across the rails
events.E2: P4: he looks up at the office clock; his balloon
events.E3: P5: she walks off down the platform; 'Much obliged!' tailed to her
events.E4: P6: the cupboard open in the right window, the key on its hook on the door leaf
events.E5: P7: pencil to chin before the open cupboard; his line; the SERVICE door shut (caption)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the far view fills panel by panel; each balloon arrives after its panel, its tail stretched across the rails
beat_frames: b01: P1 (establishing far view, agent at desk)
b04: P3 balloon laid across the rails (question)
b05: + P4 with answer, + P5 without balloon
b08: P7 forgetting balloon laid (= the page)

self_check.viewer: every panel framed from beyond two tracks: our platform's painted edge at the foot of each frame, rails between, figures about 100 px tall in a station 530 px wide; panel 1's near lamp post and bench give the scale
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
self_check.texture_check: 100 % crops of the station and the trees (panels 1 and 5) show rock grain, hatching strokes and cut or torn card edges on every card; no region is a flat or gradient fill
self_check.evidence: measured (size, pixel checks named in the repair) and judged from the full-size page by the repair maker; a fresh blind reading of the repair is pending

weaknesses: the figures and the tiny interior set are small at this distance (about 100 px), so their rubbing and hatching read as tone rather than as strokes
the hatching is generated (sine stripes broken by noise) rather than drawn stroke by stroke; at 100 % it reads as charcoal hatching, at phone width as grain
the 0.95 px softening, needed for the JPEG budget, takes the finest charcoal dust off
licence_note: the page uses the CC BY-SA 3.0 Cueva de las manos texture (Suzko) as rubbing on every card and in the sky: the page image is an adaptation and is released under CC BY-SA 3.0 with attribution to Suzko

changed: every card rebuilt with the charcoal-card kit: rock rub from the foraged Cueva relief, broken charcoal hatching, cut or torn card edges, per-card shadows
trees replaced by varied hand-cut shapes (round, poplar, fir, bush) in place of repeated polygons; a second torn ridge of hills
sky, ballast, interior and window light no longer smooth gradients: rubbed and hatched
repairs.pass_test: at a 100% crop of the station and trees, charcoal grain and card edges are visible, and no region is a flat gradient fill
